thread:
alex: Heads up — after pushing the kernel+driver+fw combo to eu-west canary (nodes gpu-node-eu1-04[0-5]) we've seen a spike in corrected ECC counts and an increase in Xid 62 GPU resets. Alert fired at 11:23 UTC.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] gpu-node-eu1-042: gpu.reset Xid=62 x3 in 5m, corrected_ecc > baseline (3x). Link: https://ops.redwood/alerts/1876543210

maya: Reproduced on 042, dmesg shows repeated lines: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 62, GPU has fallen off the bus` followed by kernel oops on nv_peer_memory.

omar: Quick data point — the canary was 12 nodes (10% of eu-west GPU fleet). All nodes had driver v525.85, fw 2.1.8, kernel 6.1.24. Previous stable was driver v520.x + fw 2.1.6 + kernel 5.15.

raj: Any correlation with network fabric? last night we saw microbursting on br-ex0 in eu-west-1 around the same window. Could be PCI enumeration timing + driver change.

maya: I pulled `nvidia-smi -q` from affected host: `GPU 0: ECC errors (corrected): 124 -> baseline was 12`. Noticed CRC errs on PCIe as well.

alex: Dumped kernel logs, snippet: ```
[23456.789012] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 62, GPU has fallen off the bus
[23456.789045] pci 0000:65:00.0: BAR 0: failed to map resource: -12
[23456.789200] kernel: nv_peer_memory: probe failed
```

dana: We should pause the rollout. Proposal: mark canary nodes cordoned, drain new jobs, and revert driver on the rest of eu-west canary pool to v520 while we triage 042-045.

omar: Agree. Also want to increase telemetry sampling to full (100%) for KV cache and pci counters on the cordoned hosts for next 6 hours. Need to flip `telemetry.sampling.gpu=1.0` via `cfgpush` on the 12 nodes.

raj: If network microbursts are contributing, also add `pci=retries=8` kernel boot param to canary nodes for a test run? We can hotpatch on a single node by remove+insert driver with `modprobe -r nvidia` then `modprobe nvidia nv_peermem=0` to disable peer mem and see if Xids stop.

maya: I can run a hotpatch on gpu-node-eu1-045 now and monitor. Will post before/after stats.

infra-bot: Deploy job #4578: cordon/drain initiated for gpu-node-eu1-043..045 — progress 3/3.

maya: Hotpatch done on 045: `modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia nv_peer_mem=0`. Immediately saw corrected ECC counts stop rising. No new Xid in 12m.

alex: Good signal. That narrows to nv_peer_mem interactions + new driver/fw/kernel timing. For rollback plan: revert driver to v520 on canary hosts, reprovision fw 2.1.6 on them, keep kernel at 6.1.24 for parity, and run 24h soak.

dana: Can we capture a full capture of PCIe counters, `lspci -vv` and `ethtool -S` around the time window to share with hw vendor? I'll open a ticket with vendor and attach logs: PCIe CRC err, ECC histogram, driver dmesg.

raj: Opening vendor ticket now — ticket #HW-9931 included. Attaching `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q`, `smart` logs. Recommend we also schedule a fw downgrade window.

omar: One more ask — add a temporary automatic fallback in router policy to route high-load inference traffic off eu-west GPU pool by 20% while we validate. Minimizes customer impact.

alex: Action items: 1) Pause rollout (dana) 2) Revert driver on canary and fw where possible (dana/raj) 3) Increase telemetry on cordoned nodes (omar) 4) Hotpatch test on 045 confirmed (maya) 5) Vendor ticket (raj) 6) Route fallback reduce load (alex)

maya: I'll keep monitoring 045 and post 1h and 3h snapshots. If Xid returns after re-enabling `nv_peer_mem`, that confirms peer path bug.

oncall-bot: [INFO] Incident tracked in #incident-1876543210, severity: minor, assigned: eng-sre oncall.

alex: Thanks all — holding the canary. We'll reconvene after vendor replies or 6h soak. :hourglass:
